claim.why_it_matters: In the second bit-alignment figure (the GROUP-USAGE BIT variant of group-1), the PICTURE clause 'pic 1' has been dropped from item-4. Without it the entry no longer describes a boolean item at all, yet the figure still charts one occupied bit position for item-4 at bit 1 of byte 5. The same entry is written 'pic 1 usage BIT.' in the first figure on the same page, so the transcription is internally inconsistent and the example as transcribed would not compile.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed by rendering PDF page 1101 (printed folio 1071) at 300 dpi and cropping/upscaling the second code figure 2x. The glyphs on the item-4 line of the second figure read unambiguously: '02  item-4  pic 1 usage BIT.' followed by a single '1' under bit position 1 and '5' in the 'Byte # in data item' column. The tokens 'pic' and '1' are clearly legible between 'item-4' and 'usage'; there is no wrapping, no continuation line, and no adjacent line onto which 'pic 1' could have reflowed - the very next printed line is '02  group-2 GROUP-USAGE BIT.'. The transcription in specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 44257 reads '   02  item-4  usage BIT.          1                  5' with 'pic 1' absent, so this is real content loss and not page-break furniture, line wrapping, hyphenation, or whitespace normalization. Both quotations in the claim are faithful: the PDF quote matches the rendered glyphs (modulo intra-line spacing, which is immaterial) and the markdown quote is verbatim from specs/ISO_COBOL.md:44257 and from the extracted page-1101.md line 38. The internal-inconsistency argument also checks out: the SAME entry in the first figure on the same page is transcribed correctly as '02  item-4  pic 1 usage BIT.' (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:44236), and the two figures are deliberately identical for item-1 through item-4 - the whole point of the second figure is that only group-2 changes (it gains GROUP-USAGE BIT), so item-4 must be identical in both. Meaning IS changed: with no PICTURE clause, 'item-4 usage BIT' is not a valid elementary boolean data description entry, yet the bit chart on that same line still shows exactly one occupied bit at byte 5 bit 1 - the chart now contradicts the code it annotates, and a reader deriving USAGE BIT / GROUP-USAGE BIT alignment rules from this normative example is given a self-contradictory entry. Sole caveat on the claim's wording: the leading '1-5' total for group-1 and the downstream implicit-filler line '02 PIC 1(2)' are transcribed correctly, so the damage is confined to the single dropped 'pic 1' token.
verdict.corrected_description: Confirmed as described. specs/ISO_COBOL.md:44257 drops the 'pic 1' PICTURE clause from the item-4 entry in the second bit-alignment figure on page 1101 (printed folio 1071). PDF: '   02  item-4  pic 1 usage BIT.    1                  5'. Markdown: '   02  item-4  usage BIT.          1                  5'. The fix is to restore 'pic 1' so the line matches the corresponding, correctly transcribed entry in the first figure at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:44236.
